title: DataAccessV1dot1
description: K-05 v1.1, a minor version of the data-access calls (T-071; 02-contracts K-05: 'v1.1 at F3 adds the effect calls'; 02-contracts section 9 F3). It only adds to v1 (data-access.v1.schema.json, frozen and unchanged, referred to here): every v1 definition is here under its own name, unchanged ones by reference; the changed ones take new optional fields or more enum values, so every v1 exchange is a v1.1 exchange. Added: the calls that write and run K-07 v1's effect rows (effects in the commit's and a firing's writes; claimEffects, recordEffectResult, serviceBack; reconciliationRefund) and record a provider event once (recordProviderEvent); the outbox claim's write, renewal and re-claim in K-07's outbox_claims (claimOutbox's claim, renewClaim) and the moves K-07 v1 leaves to K-05 v1.1 (markRow waitingChat, the commit's moves of waiting rows, dispatcherGivesUp, markPart failed's Retry-After and message id, markPart's row state and version, a wrong-state error); and the rows that follow a failed row (arch 02 line 125; K-07 followUp): the next way or the owner's number with dispatcherGivesUp, a failed safety line's other ways with markPart failed, and the one short 'all set' (writeAllSet), each with its event-log entries in the same transaction; and the event-log entries of each effect result (recordEffectResult events). The tables they read and write are K-04 v1's core tables and K-07 v1's schema addition (outbox-effects.v1.tables.json: effects, provider_events, outbox_claims). Not model-facing, so number and length limits are schema rules here. Owner: the architect.

writes.title: Writes
writes.description: Everything one turn commits, all or nothing, in one transaction under the turn id (arch 01 lines 39 to 41; arch 02 line 121; 02-contracts K-05 item 1): state writes, open questions opened or closed, clock rows made or cancelled, outbox rows with no plan yet, reservations confirmed or released, and event-log entries. Every list is present, empty when the turn has none. From v1.1 (T-071) two more lists may be given, each left out when the turn has none, so every v1 commit is a v1.1 commit: effects (effect rows written pending after the state writes, and effects in outage let go) and waitingChat (waiting rows superseded or withdrawn).

commitResult.title: CommitResult
commitResult.description: What a commit (or a clock's firing) wrote: each row it inserted or updated with its version after the commit (turn, outbox and event-log rows left out), the turn's outbox rows with their commit order, and any next in line its releases promoted. A repeat writes nothing, so its written and promoted are empty, while outboxRows still lists the turn's rows, read back by turn id (K-04 keeps no copy of a commit's result). From v1.1 (T-071): the effect rows written or let go are listed in written (table effects, with their version), and waitingChat lists the waiting rows the commit ended, with their versions after the move (left out when the commit ended none; empty on a repeat).

commitTurn.request.title: CommitTurnRequest
commitTurn.request.description: Commit a turn: the gate has passed limits 1 to 6, and one transaction writes the turn row (committed), the state, open questions, clock rows, outbox rows, reservations and the event log under the turn id, all or nothing, once (arch 01 lines 39 to 41; arch 02 line 121; arch 10 line 508; 02-contracts K-05 item 1). v1.1 (T-071): its writes may also hold effects and waitingChat (writes).

versionsRead.description: Every row the turn's decisions and read-backs rest on, at the version read; each is compared, written or not (limit 4: 'Compare-and-set on every row the read-back showed', arch 06 line 305).

commitTurn.response.title: CommitTurnResponse
commitTurn.response.description: Committed. A repeat of a committed turn id writes nothing and returns the first commit's turn id, time and outbox rows with repeated true, whatever the repeat's body (tour line 418; arch 10 line 508: a crash or retry never doubles an effect).

commitTurn.errors.title: CommitTurnErrors
commitTurn.errors.description: Refused, nothing written: the rows that changed (limit 4), the reservation no longer held (limit 5), the turn already parked (it never commits: arch 11 line 576), a database rule, or a transient failure. v1.1 adds wrongState: an effect let go that is not in outage.

claimedRow.title: ClaimedRow
claimedRow.description: A claimed outbox row: what the dispatcher needs to run limit 8 and send it (arch 06 line 313; arch 02 line 125). From v1.1 (T-071), two more fields, always written by a v1.1 call: claim, the claim this call took (K-07 outboxClaim, outbox_claims), and claimedFrom, the state the row was claimed from.

version.description: The row's version after the claim; marks compare it.

versionsRead.description: Limit 8 checks them unchanged at send (arch 06 line 313).

claim.description: The claim taken (K-07 outboxClaim; outbox_claims): claimer and claimedAt this call's, lapsesAt claimedAt + 60 s (K-07 default 2), claimNo raised from the row's last claim, and firstTryAt and nextTryNotBefore kept from it (null at a first claim), so the 15 minutes before the next way still count from the first try and a pending Retry-After still holds (arch 02 line 125; arch 10 line 540).

claimedFrom.description: checked (planned and checked), held (its held_until passed) or sending (a claim that lapsed, taken again): K-07's moves checked, held or sending to sending by claimOutbox.

passedHeld.description: Rows held for text hours that later rows passed (arch 02 line 125).

markPart.request.title: MarkPartRequest
markPart.request.description: What happened to one part (02-contracts K-05 item 3): another send under the same key after a timeout or crash (attempt), accepted by the provider with its ids (sent), its delivery receipt (delivered: arch 02 line 127), or a reported failure (failed: the next try gets a new key, arch 01 line 65). A part is named by its key, or a receipt by the provider's message id (K-04 outbox_parts_linq_message_idx). v1.1 (T-071): a failure may carry the provider's message id and the provider's Retry-After as nextTryNotBefore, and a safety line's first failure the rows that take it every other way at once (followUps, with their events).

providerMessageId.description: The provider's message id (K-04 outbox_parts.linq_message_id; K-11 names its form).

providerOptionIds.description: For a poll, the provider's option ids (K-04 outbox_parts.linq_option_ids), else null.

errorCode.description: The provider's error code, such as 4001 or 4006 (K-04 outbox_parts.error_code).

retry.description: Whether a next try follows (section 07's rules, K-07): true makes the next key, try + 1.

providerMessageId.description: The provider's message id when the failure report carries one (a 4001 or 4006 response): stored in outbox_parts.linq_message_id when the part has none, so a delivery receipt that comes after all finds the part (arch 01 line 65; K-07 open gap 13; the database engineer's review of K-07). Left out or null: none given. New in v1.1.

nextTryNotBefore.description: The provider's Retry-After as a time: the next try waits until then (arch 10 line 540: 'each try after any Retry-After'). Stored in outbox_claims.next_try_not_before, so a dispatcher that claims the row again after a lapse sends no earlier (K-07 rule 6); renewClaim refuses a try before it and clears it when the try goes. Only with retry true. Left out or null: none given. New in v1.1.

followUps.description: A failed safety line goes at once every other way the person allows (arch 02 line 125: 'A failed safety line retries every 10 s for 15 minutes and goes at once every other way the person allows'; RULES 4.12; K-07 retry rule 3, followUp safetyOtherWay): the rows for those ways, written planned under the failed row's turn, bundle and trace id in the same transaction as this failure, so the failure is never recorded without them. Given with the safety line's first reported failure only, and only for a row whose send class is safety (code checks: C-126); its retries every 10 s carry none. Left out: none. New in v1.1.

events.description: With followUps: their event-log entries (K-08 outbox_row.created, one per row, whose why names the failed row and the follow-up kind: the link K-07 open gap 3 keeps in the event log), carrying the failed row's turn id, trace id and bundle. Left out with followUps. New in v1.1.

markPart.response.title: MarkPartResponse
markPart.response.description: Marked. A repeat (a second receipt, a second 'sent' for the same key) changes nothing and says repeated. firstDelivery is true on the row's first delivery receipt, so the caller arms the question's clock (arch 02 line 127; armClock). v1.1 (T-071) adds row: markPart moves the row with its parts in the same transaction (K-07 'How K-05 v1's calls use them': the last part accepted, sending to sent; every part's latest try delivered, to delivered; failed with retry on a part of a sent row, back to checked) and raises the row's version by one whenever it changes a part, so the dispatcher compares the new version in its next markRow (the database engineer's review of K-07).

nextKey.description: After a failure with retry, the next try's key; else null.

row.description: The row after the mark: its state in K-07's words and its version. Always written by a v1.1 call.

followUpRows.description: The follow-up rows a failure with followUps wrote, with the commit order the database gave them; left out when it wrote none (a repeat writes none). New in v1.1.

markPart.errors.title: MarkPartErrors
markPart.errors.description: notFound; transient; and from v1.1 wrongState: the part is not in a state the mark starts from (K-07 partMove), such as sent for a failed part; and constraint: a follow-up row the database refuses (a row id already taken, 23505; a handle or person that does not exist, 23503), so nothing, the failure included, was written.

markRow.request.title: MarkRowRequest
markRow.request.description: Limit 8's outcome for a claimed row (arch 06 line 313; 02-contracts K-05 item 3): held until a time (outside text hours: 9am, or 8am for owner and team), dropped as stopped (its question takes step 9's never-delivered path), stale (its plan and final parts are cleared so it is composed again from today's record, S13-57), or withdrawn (its booking or question has closed). v1.1 (T-071) adds waitingChat: a customer mobile with no open chat, so the row waits with no claim, no clock and no held_until until the mobile texts in (arch 06 line 313; RULES 4.1b; MC C9; K-07 waiting_chat): the move clears held_until and deletes the row's outbox_claims row. Whether the chat is open is the caller's read (K-05 v1.2's recipient send state).

heldUntil.description: For held, until when (K-04 outbox_rows.held_until); null otherwise.

markRow.response.title: MarkRowResponse
markRow.response.description: Marked: the row's new version and the outcome (v1.1 adds waitingChat).

markRow.errors.title: MarkRowErrors
markRow.errors.description: versionChanged; notFound; transient; and from v1.1 wrongState: the row is not sending (limit 8's outcomes start only from sending: K-07 rowMove).

fireClock.request.title: FireClockRequest
fireClock.request.description: Fire a clock row once, together with what its firing commits, in one transaction: the row goes from armed to fired, and the safe default's writes (the step's clock branch, after the gate) commit with it, so a crash never fires twice or loses the default (02-contracts K-05 item 5; arch 02 line 127; arch 10 lines 508, 540). Staging's 'Fire now' calls this same path (BP 9.4). Per QUESTIONS.md NQ-RT-4's default the firing is a turn on the handle's actor (or a sweep job for a row with no handle) whose only input is the clock row: 'turn' is that turn's row, needed when the writes include outbox rows (K-04 outbox_rows.turn_id is not null); the event log carries jobId. v1.1 (T-071): its writes may also hold effects and waitingChat (writes).

by.description: alarm: the handle actor's alarm; sweep: the minute sweep; fireNow: staging's test console, which may fire before the due time (BP 9.4).

jobId.description: The firing's job id for the event log (K-04 event_log.job_id: 'For a clock firing ...').

turn.description: The firing's turn row, or null when its writes hold no outbox row. Its handle is the clock row's.

fireClock.response.title: FireClockResponse
fireClock.response.description: Fired, once. A repeat writes nothing and returns the first firing's time, turn and outbox rows with repeated true.

fireClock.errors.title: FireClockErrors

oneOf.title: NotArmedError
oneOf.description: Still waiting (never armed) or cancelled: nothing fires.

oneOf.title: NotDueError
oneOf.description: firedAt is before the due time and the caller is not 'fireNow'.

fireClock.errors.description: v1.1 adds wrongState: an effect let go that is not in outage.

wrongStateError.title: WrongStateError
wrongStateError.description: The row is not in a state this move starts from (K-07 v1's allowed moves: outbox-effects README 'Allowed moves'): markRow on a row that is no longer sending, markPart sent on a part that is not pending, renewClaim for a part that is not pending, a result for an effect that is not running, a commit letting go an effect that is not in outage, or an 'all set' for a row that is not failed (writeAllSet). Nothing was written; state is where the row stands now (the database engineer's review of K-07 v1: markRow and markPart need a wrong-state error). New in v1.1.

rowId.description: The outbox row's id, the part's idempotency key, or the effect id.

state.description: Its state now, in K-07's words.

claimLostError.title: ClaimLostError
claimLostError.description: The caller no longer holds the claim: its claim lapsed and another dispatcher or effects runner claimed the row again, or the row left the claimed state (K-07 README 'How a claim lapses'). Nothing was written; the caller stops working on the row, so a send or a try is never doubled (arch 11 line 576). New in v1.1.

claimer.description: Who holds it now, or null.

claimNo.description: For an outbox row, the claim number now (outbox_claims.claim_no), or null; effects carry no claim number.

state.description: The row's state now, in K-07's words.

effectNew.title: EffectNew
effectNew.description: An effect row a commit, a clock firing or the daily reconciliation writes (K-07 v1 effectRow; outbox-effects.v1.tables.json effects; arch 10 line 508: 'Stripe and calendar calls run from effect rows'). The call adds the rest: turn_id (the commit's or the firing's turn) or job_id (a firing with no turn, or the reconciliation job), state pending, tries 0, runs 1, and no claim, first try, provider id, error or ledger line (the table's defaults). The fields and each kind's rules are K-07's effectRow. New in v1.1.

effectId.description: The effect id: reconciliation matches each Stripe charge and refund to its ledger line by it (arch 10 line 550).

businessId.description: The business it is for (arch 10 line 546); null for a Linq contact, which belongs to Rosie's one number.

bookingId.description: The booking it is about, or null.

port.description: The port it runs through: stripe (K-14), calendar (K-16) or linq (K-11).

calendarProvider.description: For a calendar effect, google or microsoft (MC 8 'Calendars'; K-16); null otherwise.

visitId.description: For a calendar effect, the visit (arch 05 line 267: one event per visit, keyed by booking id, visit and person); K-30 names the visit row.

personId.description: For a calendar effect, the booked person whose calendar holds the event (arch 05 line 267); for a Stripe effect, the payer or the person refunded; null otherwise.

handleId.description: For linq_contact_add, the mobile's handle (K-04 handles; arch 11 line 572); null otherwise.

amount.description: For a charge, refund, pay link or monthly charge, the amount in whole cents (CQ-09); null otherwise.

portRequest.description: The request in the port's terms (02-contracts K-07: 'the request in the port's terms'). Its shape is the port contract's (K-14, K-16, K-11), open until each freezes; never a key or a card number (rule 7; arch 02 line 109).

idempotencyKey.description: One idempotency key over all its tries (arch 10 line 542: 'retry network errors 5 times in 10 minutes on one idempotency key'). Unique.

effectLetGo.title: EffectLetGo
effectLetGo.description: An effect in its service's outage that the turn lets go: outage to cancelled, K-07's letGo move ('Still down with no yes: let go': arch 11 line 582; S12-17). It never runs. Refused with wrongState when the effect is not in outage, and versionChanged when its version moved (the service came back and it ran again). New in v1.1.

effectWrites.title: EffectWrites
effectWrites.description: The effect rows a commit writes and lets go (K-07 'Allowed moves': (new) to pending by commitTurn or fireClock; outage to cancelled by letGo). Both lists present, empty when there are none. New in v1.1.

waitingChatWrites.title: WaitingChatWrites
waitingChatWrites.description: Outbox rows waiting for a chat to open (K-07 state waiting_chat) that this commit ends (K-07 'Allowed moves'; arch 06 line 313; RULES 4.1b; K-07 defaults 9 and 10). supersede: the commit of the turn that answers a mobile's first text writes the one message giving each booking as it stands (answerRowId, one of this commit's outboxRows, to recipientHandleId: a code check), and every waiting_chat row to that handle moves to superseded. withdrawForBookings and withdrawForQuestions: every waiting_chat row about a booking or open question this commit closes moves to withdrawn. The call finds the rows itself, under FOR UPDATE, so none is missed, and appends one event-log entry per row moved (K-08 kind outbox_row.state_changed; old state waiting_chat, the new state, and why: the answer row or the booking or question closed; id '<row id>/superseded' or '<row id>/withdrawn'), carrying the commit's turn id, trace id and bundle (or the firing's job id). New in v1.1.

answerRowId.description: The one message this commit writes to it (K-07 followUp chatOpenAnswer).

followUpRow.title: FollowUpRow
followUpRow.description: A row written because an earlier row failed (arch 02 line 125; K-07 v1 followUp, retry rules 3 and 5): why is K-07's follow-up kind (nextWay: the next way the person allows after the row failed for 15 minutes, such as an email row with no copyOfRowId, S12-10; ownerGetsNumber: none left, so the owner gets the number to call, S12-10; safetyOtherWay: a failed safety line also goes at once every other way the person allows, RULES 4.12), and row is the new outbox row as a commit writes one, with no plan. The call writes it planned under the failed row's turn id, bundle and trace id (K-04 outbox_rows.turn_id is not null; no turn of its own is needed, since K-04 turns are written by texts), with commit_seq from K-04's identity column, so it comes after every row committed before. Written by dispatcherGivesUp (nextWay, ownerGetsNumber) and markPart failed (safetyOtherWay). New in v1.1.

renewClaim.request.title: RenewClaimRequest
renewClaim.request.description: The dispatcher is about to send one part under its key (a first send, or a retry): renew the claim and record the try (K-07 README 'How a claim lapses': renewed by 60 s at each part attempt, default 2; outboxClaim firstTryAt: 'Written by the dispatcher at its first send'; nextTryNotBefore: 'cleared when the try goes'). New in v1.1.

claimer.description: The dispatcher that claimed it (claimOutbox claimer).

claimNo.description: The claim number its claim gave (claimedRow claim.claimNo).

idempotencyKey.description: The part about to go: one of this row's parts, pending.

renewClaim.response.title: RenewClaimResponse
renewClaim.response.description: Renewed: lapsesAt is at + 60 s; firstTryAt is set to at if it was null and kept otherwise; nextTryNotBefore is cleared. The outbox row's own version does not change (the claim is its own row, outbox_claims, with its own version), so the caller's next markRow still compares the row's version.

renewClaim.errors.title: RenewClaimErrors
renewClaim.errors.description: claimLost: the row is not sending, or its claim is another's (a lapsed claim the caller did not renew in time and another dispatcher took): the caller sends nothing. notYet: the provider's Retry-After has not passed (K-07 rule 6). wrongState: the part is not this row's or not pending. notFound; transient. Nothing was written.

dispatcherGivesUp.request.title: DispatcherGivesUpRequest
dispatcherGivesUp.request.description: Sends still failing after 15 minutes of tries: the row ends failed and, in the same transaction, the rows that follow it are written: the next way the person allows (such as an email row), or with none left one row to the owner with the number to call (arch 02 line 125; S12-09, S12-10; K-07 move sending to failed by dispatcherGivesUp, retry rule 5, followUp nextWay and ownerGetsNumber). The 15 minutes count from the claim's firstTryAt (K-07 rule 5), never from a part's attempts. New in v1.1.

followUps.description: The rows that follow the failed one (K-07 followUp): nextWay, one row for each next way the person allows, or, with none left, one ownerGetsNumber row to the owner (S12-10: 'With no email on file, Sam gets the number to call'). Each is written planned under the failed row's turn, bundle and trace id (K-04 outbox_rows.turn_id is not null), so unplannedRows lists it with that turn's rows and it is composed and checked as any row is (writePlan). Empty only when no follow-up applies: a safety line whose other ways already went at its first failure (markPart failed followUps), or a row to the owner with no other way left, for whom the sources name no one to give the number to (open gap 13). Which ways the person allows is the caller's read (K-05 v1.2's recipient send state): a code check (C-126).

events.description: The event-log entries of this give-up (arch 09 line 457: every write appends): the row's move to failed (K-08 outbox_row.state_changed, old state sending, new state failed, why: 15 minutes of tries since firstTryAt), and one outbox_row.created per follow-up row whose why names the failed row and the follow-up kind (the link K-07 open gap 3 keeps in the event log). The call writes them with the failed row's turn id, trace id and bundle.

dispatcherGivesUp.response.title: DispatcherGivesUpResponse
dispatcherGivesUp.response.description: Failed: the row's new version, the claim's firstTryAt the 15 minutes counted from, and the follow-up rows written with the commit order the database gave them (after every row committed before; K-04 commit_seq). The claim row stays as the record of the tries; parts keep their states.

dispatcherGivesUp.errors.title: DispatcherGivesUpErrors
dispatcherGivesUp.errors.description: tooSoon: no part has gone yet (firstTryAt null), or fewer than 15 minutes have passed since it; claimLost; wrongState (not sending); versionChanged (a repeat of a give-up already made); constraint: a follow-up row the database refuses (a row id already taken, 23505; a handle or person that does not exist, 23503); notFound; transient. Nothing was written: neither the move to failed nor any follow-up row.

claimedEffect.title: ClaimedEffect
claimedEffect.description: An effect row the effects runner now holds: the row as it stands after the claim (K-07 effectRow, running), its version, the state it was claimed from, and the claim (outbox-effects.v1.tables.json effects.claimed_by and claim_lapses_at). New in v1.1.

claimedFrom.description: pending (claimEffects: a new run), running (claimEffects: a claim that lapsed, taken again, the run's tries and first try kept) or outage (serviceBack: the run after the outage).

claimEffects.request.title: ClaimEffectsRequest
claimEffects.request.description: Claim effect rows to run (02-contracts K-05 v1.1: 'claim effect rows'; arch 10 line 508): pending rows, and running rows whose claim lapsed (a runner that died: K-07 README 'How a claim lapses'), oldest first. Rows in outage wait for serviceBack. It takes no event-log entries: it picks its rows itself (SKIP LOCKED), so the caller cannot name them, and K-08 v1 has no kind for a claim; the run it starts is logged by each result (recordEffectResult events, old state running with its tries, runs and first try), and a log entry for the claim itself is open gap 15. New in v1.1.

claimer.description: The effects runner instance, for traces (BP 5.5).

ports.description: Only these ports' rows; left out: every port.

items.description: The port an effect runs through: stripe (K-14), calendar (K-16) or linq (K-11) (K-07 effectRow.port).

claimEffects.response.title: ClaimEffectsResponse
claimEffects.response.description: The rows claimed, each now running under this claimer until claimLapsesAt. A pending row starts a run: firstTryAt is now and tries 0 (K-07 effectRow: 'When the current run's first try went, at its claim'). A lapsed running row keeps its tries, runs and firstTryAt. Empty when nothing is due.

serviceBack.request.title: ServiceBackRequest
serviceBack.request.description: A service is back after its outage: claim its effect rows in outage so each runs once more on its same key (arch 11 line 582: 'Charges and refunds wait, then run once'; S12-16, S12-18; K-07 move outage to running by serviceBack). Whether the service is back is the runtime's (C-174 to C-176). Like claimEffects it takes no event-log entries (open gap 15): the new run shows in each result's entry (runs raised, tries from 0). New in v1.1.

port.description: The port an effect runs through: stripe (K-14), calendar (K-16) or linq (K-11) (K-07 effectRow.port).

serviceBack.response.title: ServiceBackResponse
serviceBack.response.description: The rows claimed, oldest first: each starts a new run (runs + 1, tries 0, firstTryAt now) and is running under this claimer.

recordEffectResult.request.title: RecordEffectResultRequest
recordEffectResult.request.description: Record one try's outcome on a running effect (02-contracts K-05 v1.1: 'record an effect's result'; arch 10 line 542): ok (succeeded: the provider's object id, and the ledger line when there is one); networkError (retried on the same key; nextTryAt is when the runner tries next, null when it plans none); declined (a card decline, never retried: RULES 3.11). Every result is logged in the same transaction (events). New in v1.1.

providerObjectId.description: For ok, the provider's id of what it made or changed (effects.provider_object_id), or null; null otherwise.

errorCode.description: For networkError and declined, the error the network or provider gave (effects.error_code); null for ok.

ledgerLineId.description: For ok, the ledger line it writes or matches, when the caller has one (K-07 open gap 14); null otherwise.

nextTryAt.description: For networkError, when the next try goes, within 10 minutes of the run's first try: the claim lapses 60 s after it; null otherwise.

events.description: The try's event-log entries, appended in the same transaction as the result (arch 09 lines 457, 492: every write appends who, what, old to new, when and why; K-08 kind effect.result): at least the effect's own entry, actor job (the effects runner), old and new state, tries and error, and why (the try's outcome; on the run's 5th failed try, the service's outage). The call writes them with the effect's turn id, or its job id when it has no turn, and its trace id (K-04 event_log_turn_or_job), and the turn's bundle (null for a job). The runner's span for the call is K-08's effectRun, not an entry here.

recordEffectResult.response.title: RecordEffectResultResponse
recordEffectResult.response.description: Recorded: tries rose by one. ok: succeeded. declined: declined. networkError: still running, the claim renewed to nextTryAt + 60 s (at + 60 s when nextTryAt is null); or, when this was the run's 5th try, outage, that service's outage row (arch 10 line 542; S12-16; K-07 default 3). Leaving running clears the claim (claimLapsesAt null).

recordEffectResult.errors.title: RecordEffectResultErrors
recordEffectResult.errors.description: claimLost (another runner holds it); wrongState (not running); versionChanged (a repeat of a recorded result, compared and set as markRow is); notFound; transient. Nothing was written.

recordProviderEvent.request.title: RecordProviderEventRequest
recordProviderEvent.request.description: Store a Stripe or calendar event once by (provider, provider event id), after the gateway verified it (02-contracts K-05 v1.1: 'record a provider event once by its event id'; arch 02 line 109: 'Stripe and calendar events go to PostgreSQL ... Known event id: 200, dropped'). The request is K-07 v1's providerEvent. New in v1.1.

recordProviderEvent.response.title: RecordProviderEventResponse
recordProviderEvent.response.description: Recorded once. A known (provider, provider event id) writes nothing and answers repeated true with the stored row's receivedAt and effectId, whatever the repeat's body: the gateway answers 200 and drops it (arch 02 line 109).

recordProviderEvent.errors.title: RecordProviderEventErrors
recordProviderEvent.errors.description: constraint: a business or effect id that does not exist (23503), or a K-07 CHECK (23514); transient: the write failed, so the gateway answers 503 and the provider retries (arch 02 line 109). Nothing was written.

reconciliationRefund.request.title: ReconciliationRefundRequest
reconciliationRefund.request.description: The daily reconciliation, a job with no turn, writes the refund of a charge with no agreed booking behind it, at once (arch 10 line 550: 'with no agreed booking behind it, refunded at once and both told'; S12-26; K-07 move (new) to pending by reconciliationJob, a stripe_refund only, with bookingId null: K-07 default 12), with its event-log entries carrying the job id (K-04 event_log_turn_or_job). The ledger line, and telling both, are not this call's (K-28; a turn). New in v1.1.

jobId.description: The reconciliation run's job id (effects.job_id; K-04 event_log.job_id).

reconciliationRefund.response.title: ReconciliationRefundResponse
reconciliationRefund.response.description: Written, pending, for the effects runner. The effect id is the key: the job run again over the same 48 hours answers repeated true with the stored row's version and writes nothing, whatever the repeat's body, so a charge is never refunded twice.

reconciliationRefund.errors.title: ReconciliationRefundErrors
reconciliationRefund.errors.description: constraint: another effect already holds the idempotency key (23505 effects_idempotency_key_key), or a business or person id that does not exist (23503); transient. Nothing was written.

writeAllSet.request.title: WriteAllSetRequest
writeAllSet.request.description: Texts work again for a person whose rows failed and went another way: write the one short 'all set' (arch 02 line 125: 'once texts work, one short "all set"'; S12-10: 'Once texts work, a short "all set" goes out. Nothing already emailed is sent again in full'). Called by the dispatcher (C-126). When texts count as working, and so when it calls, the sources do not say (K-07 open gap 12; open gap 14 here). The row is an ordinary text row with no plan (K-07: no follow-up kind of its own), written planned under the first failed row's turn id, bundle and trace id, so it is composed and checked as any row is (writePlan); its id is fixed by rule, '<first failed row id>/all-set', so one failure set gets one 'all set'. New in v1.1.

failedRowIds.description: The failed rows to this person it closes, oldest first; each must be failed (wrongState otherwise). That they are this person's and went another way is a code check (C-126).

row.description: The 'all set' row: a text row (texts work again), never an email.

events.description: Its event-log entries (arch 09 line 457: every write appends): outbox_row.created for the row, whose why names the failed rows it closes (the link K-07 open gap 3 keeps in the event log). The call writes them with the first failed row's turn id, trace id and bundle.

writeAllSet.response.title: WriteAllSetResponse
writeAllSet.response.description: Written, planned, with the commit order the database gave it. The row id is the key: the same id again answers repeated true with the stored row and writes nothing, whatever the repeat's body, so the person gets one 'all set'.

writeAllSet.errors.title: WriteAllSetErrors
writeAllSet.errors.description: wrongState: a listed row is not failed (its state now); notFound: a listed row does not exist; constraint: a handle or person that does not exist (23503); transient. Nothing was written.
